- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots downward in next 5–7 days; apply mild upward correction or delay peak drop.
- If model forecast shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling sharply), true outcome often reverses mid-horizon; add 1–2 days of upward momentum in forecast.
- When sentiment is positive (avg > 0.1) and price is falling, model often underestimates rebound; increase forecast slope slightly or add early reversal signal.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period volatility (last 7–10 days); adjust forecast to be slightly higher in final 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “recovery” patterns (e.g., negative → positive → negative), model tends to lag in recognizing sentiment shift; align forecast with sentiment turning point 1–2 days earlier.
